elements.note: Three senses. In the foundations x̃ is the rescaled momentum at ħ, the program's sense, and FLM read the string's Y as 'a momentum coordinate' (1502.08005 §2). The dark fields, however, come from the dual momentum p̃ of a doubled phase space in which x̃ = x_L − x_R, the closed string's T-dual coordinate, has its own conjugate p̃ and fails to commute with x at a scale λ² (ħα′, ℓ_s², l_P² or 'contextual'); x̃ is then not a function of (x, p) (rank 4 in two agents' executed checks). The papers carry the first sense into the second without saying that x̃ changes status. The field-space 'conjugacy' is a heuristic induced from [x, x̃] at λ² (2212.06086 §6.4). Shared: a Lagrangian polarization of a phase space, with the dual side read as momentum. Different: one phase space at ħ against a doubled one at a string scale.

propositions.reason: 'Correlated' is the school's own word, and in most of its papers it marks a real difference from the program's gravity-only coupling, but it covers three things: (1) non-commutation of each dark field with its visible partner at a string-scale length λ ('correlated, due to their non-commutativity', 2212.06086 §6.3), with each particle paired to its dual in one metaparticle; (2) explicit non-gravitational mixing terms beyond leading order in λ (vector, scalar, fermion mass mixing, a correlated dual photon finite in the deep infrared, accelerator events), of strength never computed; (3) the observed tie of dark to baryonic mass profiles through a₀ ~ cH₀ ('via the dark energy sector'), taken from modified dark matter, whose authors allow it to emerge in ΛCDM; in the 2019 slides 'correlated' is illustrated by M_DM = M_B f(a/a₀, r/r_c, ...). At leading order, and 'to first order in the fundamental length', the sectors share only gravity, as in the program. Hübsch and Minic 2024 §5.3 state that below about 4.5×10¹⁴ GeV dark and visible matter 'interact as required, only gravitationally', which matches P4 at accessible energies; the same paper keeps the λ-correlation for a₀ and dual-SM CP phases, and its 2026 sequels neither repeat nor retract it. The contrast therefore holds against the school's main line, not against that paper at accessible energies, and the school is not consistent.

summary_line.verdict: Holds with qualification. 'Its core is published' holds: the school proposes, without derivation, that dark matter is the dual of visible matter, first publicly in a talk by Minic on 9 September 2019 and in print in Minic 2020 (single author; restated with coauthors to 2026), so '2020' dates print, not the first public statement. 'Their sector correlated with ours' uses the school's own word and holds for most of its papers, but the correlation lies beyond leading order in a string-scale length, its strength is never computed, and Hübsch and Minic 2024 state gravity-only interaction below about 4.5×10¹⁴ GeV, so the clause overstates the contrast for that paper and the school is not consistent on it. 'Neither form was found' holds for every paper read.
